related_questions.question: What are the symptoms of the current flu outbreak?

text_blocks.snippet: The current flu outbreak is characterized by symptoms such as fever or feeling feverish/chills, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, muscle or body aches, and fatigue. Some individuals may also experience vomiting and diarrhea, particularly children. Symptoms typically develop suddenly and can be more severe than a common cold.
snippet_highlighted_words: fever or feeling feverish/chills, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, muscle or body aches, and fatigue

list.snippet: Fever and Chills: A sudden increase in body temperature is common, often accompanied by chills.
Cough: A dry cough is a frequent symptom.
Sore Throat: Inflammation and pain in the throat can occur.
Runny or Stuffy Nose: Nasal congestion and discharge are also typical.
Muscle or Body Aches: Aching muscles and joints are common complaints.
Fatigue: Feeling tired and weak is a common experience.
Other Possible Symptoms: Headaches, vomiting, and diarrhea (more common in children) can also occur.
Severity: Flu symptoms are typically more intense than a cold and may include higher fever, more severe aches, and longer duration of symptoms.
When to Seek Medical Advice: Contact a doctor if symptoms worsen, persist, or if you are at risk for complications.
Distinguishing from COVID-19: While flu and COVID-19 share some symptoms, testing is necessary to determine the specific illness.

related_questions.question: What does the new flu feel like?

text_blocks.snippet: The new flu, also known as influenza, typically feels like a sudden onset of fever, body aches, headache, and fatigue. Other common symptoms include a cough, sore throat, and runny or stuffy nose. Some individuals, particularly children, may also experience vomiting and diarrhea.
snippet_highlighted_words: a sudden onset of fever, body aches, headache, and fatigue

list.title: Fever and Chills:
list.snippet: A fever is a common symptom, though not everyone experiences it. It can range from mild to high.

list.title: Body Aches and Headaches:
list.snippet: Flu can cause widespread muscle aches and pain, as well as headaches.

list.title: Fatigue:
list.snippet: Extreme tiredness and exhaustion are typical, and fatigue can linger even after other symptoms subside.

list.title: Respiratory Symptoms:
list.snippet: Coughing, sore throat, and a runny or stuffy nose are also common signs of the flu.

list.title: Gastrointestinal Issues:
list.snippet: Vomiting and diarrhea are more frequent in children but can occur in adults as well.

list.title: Onset:
list.snippet: Flu symptoms usually appear suddenly, within 1 to 7 days after exposure, with most people experiencing symptoms within 2 to 3 days.
